subject: every route under src/app/api/** that CALLS a tenancy fence, and what kind of proof its covering suites offer
method: A route fences when a CallExpression's callee is a binding imported from a fence module. An import with no call, a mention in a comment and a mention in a string are all `none` — that distinction is the defect class this census exists to measure, so it is decided by TypeScript's parser rather than by a text scan.

The fence surface grows from src/lib/auth/tenancy.ts to a fixpoint: a module that calls a fence symbol has its own exported value names marked as fence symbols, which is how the `_auth` wrappers under src/app/api/** are found without a hand-kept list. A route reaching a fence through a wrapper is `indirect` and names the hop in fenceVia.

requireTenancy and tenancyErrorResponse are the seed symbols. TenancyError is not: narrowing an error type is reading a fence, not applying one. C-507's mutation M-B deleted only the mapper and both byte-scanner suites stayed green, which is why the mapper counts.

reachesFenceModule is import-graph reach at any depth and is reported separately from `fence` on purpose. The two numbers disagree by a wide margin, and a route that reaches tenancy through a library it imports for other reasons fences on nothing.

A suite is `behavioral` when it loads the route module and calls an HTTP-method handler, `byte-scanner` when it names the route's path in a string literal and calls a file read, `none` otherwise. Where a suite does both, behavioral wins: a byte assertion beside a real response assertion is not what this census is hunting.

coverage is the strongest verdict among a route's covering suites. `byte-scanner` therefore means EVERY covering suite asserts the route by its bytes, and that is the population C-507 showed can stay green through an inverted fence.
This census ranks and does not repair. Each repair is its own backlog item so that a sweep finding twenty routes is not one change nobody reads.

mutationProof.note: A classification that was never executed is the same kind of claim this item exists against. Each sample below was proved by applying the named mutation to the route on the recorded commit and running the covering suites. The decisive direction depends on what is being proved: a `byte-scanner` or `none` row is proved when the suites stay GREEN under a mutation that breaks the fence, and a `behavioral` row is proved when the same mutation turns them RED. A `behavioral` row with no sample is a structural classification only -- this census calls a suite behavioral when it loads the route and calls a handler, which a suite that STUBS the fence also does. Sampled, not generalised -- the counts say how many of how many.

sampled.mutation: Unchanged from when this row was first sampled -- the fence DELETED: `tenancy = await requireTenancy()` replaced with a hard-coded foreign tenant, and the catch arm's `tenancyErrorResponse(err)` replaced with a 200.
sampled.evidence: 2 suites, 14 total: 10 passed / 4 skipped / 0 failed clean, and 1 FAILED with the fence deleted. The failing case is the one that asserts the route consults the fence before any tenant-scoped read and hands a refusal to the fence's own mapper.
sampled.whyItMoved: This row read `byte-scanner` and its sample proved a GAP: the same mutation left the covering suites green, 9 passed / 4 skipped, byte-identical to the clean baseline. T-484 then replaced this route's source-text case with cases that call the real handler, which moved the row to `behavioral` -- and that alone would have been a FALSE improvement in this census, because those cases stub `requireTenancy` and the fence mutation still left them green. It was measured that way before anything was recorded here. The gap is closed rather than caveated: the covering suite now asserts the refusal path, and the mutation that used to pass unnoticed fails it.

sampled.mutation: Fail OPEN: the fence still runs and its refusal path is removed -- `if (tenancyError) return tenancyErrorResponse(tenancyError)` neutered.
sampled.evidence: Same invocation as the row above: 16 passed / 0 failed, unchanged from the clean baseline.

sampled.mutation: The fence DELETED: `tenancy = await requireTenancy()` replaced with a hard-coded foreign tenant.
sampled.evidence: A routine gate scope, `jest src/__tests__/behaviors`: 120 suites / 1114 passed clean, and 120 suites / 1114 passed with the fence gone. The mutation was verified to change observable behavior rather than being a no-op -- a throwaway probe calling the handler with an unauthenticated caller answered 401 on the real route and 403 on the mutated one -- so the unchanged gate is a coverage gap and not an inert edit.

mutationProof.commit: the tower-synthesis sample was re-measured under T-484; the other two are unchanged from f383dcd6b2e668297eb40ebb751bb4f33ab34165

sampledOf.note: Sampled, not generalised. 3 of 213 fenced rows have been executed: 1 of 6 byte-scanner rows, 1 of 140 `none` rows, and 1 of 67 behavioral rows. Every other row carries the classification the parser gave it and nothing more -- which for a `behavioral` row means a suite loads the route and calls a handler, NOT that the fence was exercised.

calibration.subject: src/app/api/chat/step/route.ts
calibration.mutation: C-507's M-A: the active-tenant comparison inverted from !== to ===, so a FOREIGN clientId passes the fence and a legitimate one is refused.
calibration.result: src/__tests__/behaviors/c507-route-tenant-fence-behavior.test.ts went RED (3 failed) in the SAME jest command that left the two byte-scanner rows green, and the byte-scanner suite for that same route, src/app/api/chat/step/__tests__/route-boundary.test.ts, stayed green beside it.
calibration.why: Without this the greens below would be unreadable: a command that detects nothing proves nothing about the suites it ran. One inversion detected and two not, inside one invocation, is what makes the greens evidence.

independentReader.result: jest's own reverse-dependency reader agrees in both directions: for src/app/api/chat/step/route.ts it lists exactly the C-507 behavioral suite; for src/app/api/admin/context-layer/triage/route.ts it lists nothing.
independentReader.population: Measured over the whole census: 0 of the 140 `none` routes is imported by any test file, and 0 has its URL stem named in any of the 130 specs under tests/. The `none` verdict is therefore not an artefact of the handler-call heuristic -- nothing loads these routes at all.
